chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Know with full conviction that Allah has not fixed for any servant more than what has been specified for him in the Noble Recitation, even though his means may be great, his craving intense, and his efforts acute; nor does the weakness of a person or the paucity of his means stand in the way between what is ordained in the Noble Recitation and himself. He who realizes this and acts upon it is the best of people in comfort and benefit, while he who disregards it and doubts it exceeds all men in disadvantages. Very often a favoured person is being slowly driven (towards punishment) through those favours; and very often an afflicted person is being done good through his affliction. Therefore, O listener, increase your gratefulness, lessen your haste, and stay within the bounds of your livelihood.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between human effort and divine decree regarding livelihood in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of *al-Rizq al-Musammā* (the specifically named sustenance), asserting that no amount of human effort can exceed the divine decree allotted to each individual. This teaching underscores the Shia understanding of balancing active striving (*al-‘amal*) with spiritual contentment (*al-qana’ah*), warning that excessive pursuit of wealth may lead to being 'gradually led on' (*mustadrāj*), while trials often serve as hidden mechanisms for spiritual elevation. Consequently, the believer is urged to limit their desires to their destined portion, transforming anxiety into gratitude and patience.
